question: The north-west region of India receives rainfall in winter due to:
solution:
The correct answer is __**western disturbances**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Western disturbances** are responsible for the rainfall in the north-west region of India during winter.
 
• These are extratropical storms originating in the Mediterranean region that bring sudden winter rain and snow to the north-western parts of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Western disturbances are crucial for the Rabi crop season in India, particularly for wheat cultivation.
 
• They generally affect the weather pattern of the region from December to February.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Western disturbances typically move from west to east, crossing Iran, Afghanistan, and Pakistan before entering India.
 
• The term 'western disturbance' was coined by Indian meteorologists to describe the phenomenon.
 
• These disturbances are more frequent and stronger during La Niña years.
 
• Besides causing rainfall, they are also associated with cold waves and foggy conditions in northern India.
 
• The intensity and frequency of western disturbances can vary each year, influencing the overall winter precipitation in the region.
